title: Marriage, Divorce and Couples Therapists in Monroe County
metaTitle: Monroe County, NY Divorce and Marriage Data, With Couples Therapists
metaDescription: Monroe County courts granted 1,387 divorces in 2023 and 3,008 couples married there. The county has 144 licensed marriage and family therapists, 9.5% of New York's 1,518.
eyebrow: Data study · Rochester and Monroe County
headline: Monroe County has the second-highest number of licensed marriage and family therapists in New York (144) and the second-highest per resident: 19.2 per 100,000, against 7.6 statewide. Its courts granted 1,387 divorces in 2023, the same year 3,008 couples married in the county.

blocks.heading: What the data shows
paragraphs: Monroe County has 144 licensed marriage and family therapists (LMFTs), 9.5% of the 1,518 in New York State. The county has 3.8% of the state's residents, so it has about 2.5 times its population share of LMFTs. Only Manhattan has more (191), and only Onondaga County has more per resident (27.4 per 100,000). Erie County, with more people than Monroe, has 51. The five neighboring counties have 28 between them.

Monroe County courts granted 1,387 divorces in 2023, about 1.9 for every 1,000 residents. Across New York State the figure was 2.6. In the same year 3,008 couples married in Monroe County, about 4.0 per 1,000 residents.

Most divorces ended long marriages: 59% of Monroe County divorces in 2023 ended a marriage of 10 years or more, and 165 ended a marriage of 30 years or more. About four in ten (39%) involved at least one child under 18.

Marriages in the county have declined, from 3,587 in 2015 to 3,008 in 2023. Divorce counts were between 1,665 and 1,871 a year from 2015 to 2018. They fell sharply in 2019, as they did across New York outside New York City (29,387 in 2018, 18,701 in 2019), and have risen each year since 2021.

blocks.heading: What this means for couples
items: Rochester-area couples have more licensed marriage and family therapists nearby than most of New York: 19.2 per 100,000 residents against 7.6 statewide.

Marriage and family therapists are one of several license types that see couples. Psychologists, clinical social workers and mental health counselors may also offer couples therapy, so it is reasonable to ask any clinician about their training and experience with couples.
The five counties around Monroe have 7.7 marriage and family therapists per 100,000 residents, close to the statewide level and well below Monroe's 19.2.

Ruzicka Psychology offers [couples therapy](/specialties/couples-therapy) in Rochester. If you feel unsafe in your relationship, local help, including Willow Domestic Violence Center, is listed on our [resources page](/resources).

blocks.heading: How we counted
paragraphs: Marriages and divorces: New York State Department of Health, Vital Statistics of New York State, Table 47 (marriages by county where the ceremony took place) and Table 48 (dissolutions of marriage by county where the decree was granted), 2015 to 2023. "Divorces" on this page means all dissolutions in Table 48; in Monroe County in 2023 every one was a divorce. Length of marriage and children under 18 come from Tables 51 and 52.

Marriage and family therapists: New York State Education Department license statistics, which count licensees by the county of their mailing address as of July 1, 2026. The same counts appear in our [study of therapist supply in Monroe County](/research/monroe-county-therapists).
Rates: divorces and marriages per 1,000 residents use U.S. Census Bureau population estimates for 2023 (Vintage 2025); therapists per 100,000 use the 2025 estimates.

blocks.heading: What these numbers cannot tell you
paragraphs: Divorces are counted in the county where the court granted the decree, not where the couple lived. Some counties grant far more divorces than their own population would explain: Onondaga County granted 6,138 in 2023 (up from 1,220 in 2015) and Jefferson County 2,226 (up from 619), while Manhattan fell from 10,452 to 1,390. Some Monroe County couples may have divorced elsewhere, so county divorce rates are rough.
Marriages are counted where the ceremony took place, so wedding destinations count marriages of couples who live elsewhere.
Counts for 2021, 2022 and 2023 are marked provisional by the Department of Health. The tables do not explain the 2019 drop in divorce counts, and this page does not try to.
Licensed marriage and family therapists are counted by mailing address, which may be a home rather than an office, and a license does not mean the person is currently seeing couples.
These numbers describe how often marriages begin and end. They say nothing about why, and nothing about what helps.
